title: How a live score reaches millions of phones

hook.shape: A person sneaks a glance at a live score on a phone at work, and the question of where that number is born is left hanging.

arc: Persona hook with an open question → six steps through the write path, queue, workers and cache → the answer → callback ending

beats.summary: A person sneaks a look at a live score on a phone at work, and the question of where that number comes from is left open.
The moment on the field becomes a record with an identity, a value, the people involved and a line of commentary.
The record reaches a write endpoint; a second copy carrying the same identity is refused as a repeat, so the work happens once.
The accepted record is stored in a database and then handed to a queue as a waiting job.
Workers take jobs off the queue; one assembles a summary panel and puts it in a fast store kept close to the readers.
One notification is copied once per delivery service and then spreads to a crowd of phones that keeps growing.
At peak, many phones hit one central server at once; the request rate climbs and the node fails.
A cache layer in front takes the flood and lets one steady request through to the origin, at the cost of a short lifetime.
The chain is traced back to a person at the venue keying the result in by hand, which answers the question planted at the start.
Return to the person from the opening, now holding the answer, and close on a share line.

pacing: Open question in the first seconds, answer only near the end; keep the middle moving.
Each step grows the same board, so the flow reads as one system rather than a tour.
Slow down on the flood so the climbing rate lands, then resolve the fix in one beat.
